cohort: The study included 46 women who delivered by primary cesarean section for dystocia (cases) and 46 women who delivered vaginally (controls), all after 37 weeks of gestation.
finding: The study found no significant association between vitamin D deficiency and primary cesarean section, though a strong association between Body Mass Index (BMI) and cesarean section was observed.
mod_finding: The study found no significant association between vitamin D deficiency and primary cesarean section.
